mission.display_title: Reduce dimensions without losing the story
mission.mission_purpose: Today's Mission exists to close the deferred EDA skill from Campaign Alpha (principal component analysis) so you can reduce a complex data set's dimensionality while stating what is preserved, what is lost, and what PCA does not invent.
mission.tutor_intent: Today I will force the candidate to state the purpose of PCA in one professional sentence, name what the first components capture versus discard, and refuse treating a principal component as a causal factor. So dimensionality reduction stays exploratory craft, not magic renaming.
mission.educational_intent: Produce a cognitive move from 'many correlated variables are hard to see' to 'I can explain PCA as an exploratory reduction tool with honest limits on interpretation.'
mission.learning_objective: Explain principal component analysis as a method to reduce the dimensionality of a complex data set, and state what the components do and do not justify.
mission.concept_focus: Why reduce dimensions → what PCs capture → interpretation limits (not new causal variables).
mission.prior_bridge: Campaign Alpha closed association measures (1.2.2) under honest non-claims and deferred PCA (1.2.3). Today Volume CS1-002 opens by placing that deferred LO: exploratory judgement extends from bivariate association into multi-variable reduction.
mission.why_now: 1.2.3 is the lawful next LO after Alpha's association day; Alpha terminals named this deferral; without PCA placed now, Chapter 1 coverage remains an honest gap that recreates a syllabus cliff before distributions.
mission.expected_benefit: One closed-book PCA purpose statement plus one honest limit. Study Progress for today's Session, not Topic Complete for all of Chapter 2.
mission.explainability: Assigned as Campaign Beta Day 1 because CS1-001 deferred 1.2.3; continuity law requires the successor Volume to close that named handoff before opening 2.1.
success_criteria: Closed-book, state the purpose of PCA for a complex data set in one professional sentence.
Name what early principal components typically capture versus what later components tend to hold.
State one claim PCA does not support (e.g. that a PC is automatically a causal driver or a named business factor).
task_descriptions: Sketch 'many variables → fewer components → interpret with limits' before opening the CMP.
Complete Guided Reading through the CMP treatment of PCA for Syllabus 1.2.3.
Closed-book: purpose, capture-vs-discard, and one refused overclaim.

session.session_educational_purpose: This Session exists to execute today's Mission: build and stress-test closed-book understanding of PCA purpose and limits. Not to open univariate distributions or run a coding marathon.

knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: PCA purpose
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. In one professional sentence, what is the purpose of principal component analysis for a complex data set? Then name what early components typically capture versus what later components tend to hold.
knowledge_checks.body: Purpose first; then capture-vs-discard without formula dump.
hints: Purpose: reduce dimensionality / summarise correlated structure into fewer components.
Early PCs: major shared variation; later PCs: residual / smaller variation patterns.
knowledge_checks.explanation: PCA is an exploratory reduction tool; purpose and capture order must retrieve before interpretation theatre.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: PCA reduces the dimensionality of a complex correlated data set by summarising shared variation into fewer principal components. Early components typically capture major shared structure; later components tend to hold residual or smaller-scale variation.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Describing only 'eigenvectors' without a purpose sentence, or claiming every PC is equally meaningful.
success_criteria: Early vs later capture distinction stated.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: refuse PCA overclaim
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. A colleague says: 'PC1 is the true underlying risk factor driving claims, so we can treat it as a causal driver in the business model.' (1) What one useful thing might PC1 still be doing exploratorily? (2) State one claim this statement overreaches.
knowledge_checks.body: Allow exploratory usefulness; refuse causal / named-factor invention.
hints: Useful: summarises correlated structure / reduces noise for visualisation.
Refuse: automatic causation; automatic named business factor without external warrant.
knowledge_checks.explanation: PCA can aid exploration; it does not mint causal business factors by construction.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: PC1 may usefully summarise major shared variation among correlated variables for exploration or visualisation. It does not by itself prove a causal business driver or invent a named risk factor without external subject-matter warrant.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Accepting the causal claim, or rejecting PCA entirely as useless.
